question_text:
C₀ (eutectoid composition) ≃ 0.77 wt % C  
Cα (ferrite solubility) ≃ 0.02 wt % C  
Cθ (cementite Fe₃C) ≃ 6.67 wt % C  

Calculate the relative widths of the ferrite and carbide platelets using the lever law. Give the value of thickness ratio.
response:
## Reasoning

For pearlite at the eutectoid composition, the **lever rule** gives the mass fractions of the two phases (ferrite α and cementite θ):

$$f_\alpha = \frac{C_\theta - C_0}{C_\theta - C_\alpha}, \qquad f_\theta = \frac{C_0 - C_\alpha}{C_\theta - C_\alpha}$$

Substituting the given values:

$$f_\alpha = \frac{6.67 - 0.77}{6.67 - 0.02} = \frac{5.90}{6.65} \approx 0.887$$

$$f_\theta = \frac{0.77 - 0.02}{6.67 - 0.02} = \frac{0.75}{6.65} \approx 0.113$$

Since ferrite and cementite have nearly the same density (ρα ≈ 7.87 g/cm³, ρθ ≈ 7.70 g/cm³), the **volume fractions** ≈ mass fractions, and the thickness ratio of the platelets equals the ratio of the volume fractions:

$$\frac{t_\alpha}{t_\theta} = \frac{f_\alpha}{f_\theta} = \frac{5.90}{0.75} \approx 7.87$$

The ferrite platelets are roughly **8 times** thicker than the carbide (cementite) platelets.

$$\boxed{7.87}$$
